# Dockerfile for amg2023 HPC application
# Target: AWS CPU instance in Kubernetes

FROM ubuntu:22.04

# Set non-interactive frontend for package installations
ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive

# Configure OpenMPI for containerized environments
# Allow running as root, which is common in container scenarios
ENV OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT=1
ENV OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT_CONFIRM=1
# Use TCP for inter-container communication, disable shared memory mechanisms that may not work across nodes
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl=tcp,self
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl_vader_single_copy_mechanism=none

# Install dependencies, clone source, build, install, and clean up in a single layer
# This avoids creating unnecessary image layers, which is a best practice when not using multi-stage builds.
RUN apt-get update && \
    apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    build-essential \
    ca-certificates \
    git \
    openmpi-bin \
    libopenmpi-dev \
    libgomp1 && \
    # Clone the latest branch of the AMG source code
    git clone https://github.com/LLNL/AMG.git /opt/amg_src && \
    # FIX: Navigate to the root of the source directory to build the project correctly
    cd /opt/amg_src && \
    # FIX: Build the entire project, including required libraries, from the top-level Makefile
    make && \
    # Copy the compiled executable from its build location to a system location on the PATH
    cp test/amg /usr/local/bin/amg && \
    # Clean up the source code to reduce final image size
    cd / && \
    rm -rf /opt/amg_src && \
    # Clean up apt cache to further reduce image size
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Set a working directory for when the container starts
WORKDIR /

# Provide a default command. This can be overridden at runtime.
# Running a shell is useful for interactive debugging or launching the application with custom parameters.
CMD ["/bin/bash"]

# This MiniCluster manifest is configured to run the AMG benchmark.
# It is designed for a single-node execution on an AWS CPU instance within a Kubernetes environment.
# The job is non-interactive, and the pod will not be cleaned up upon completion to allow for log inspection.
apiVersion: flux-framework.org/v1alpha2
kind: MiniCluster
metadata:
  # A descriptive name for the MiniCluster experiment.
  name: amg2023-cpunode-test
  # Deployment will occur in the 'default' namespace as requested.
  namespace: default
spec:
  # The total number of pods in the MiniCluster job. Set to 1 for a single-node run.
  size: 1

  # The total number of MPI tasks to run. This will launch 4 processes on the single node.
  tasks: 4

  # Strict logging mode is enabled for more detailed error reporting.
  logging:
    strict: true

  # The pod and its resources will not be deleted after the job completes.
  # This is useful for debugging and inspecting logs and output.
  cleanup: false

  # Defines the application container to be run by Flux.
  containers:
    - image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/fractale-agent-experiments:amg2023
      # The main command to execute. The Flux Operator will prepend 'flux run' to this command.
      # Runs AMG with problem type 2 and a small problem size of 4x4x4 for testing purposes.
      command: amg -problem 2 -n 4 4 4

      # This is not a launcher-based job; the command is executed directly.
      # This setting MUST be false as per the instructions.
      launcher: false

# This corrected MiniCluster manifest addresses the previous failure which was likely
# an Out-Of-Memory (OOM) error caused by an excessively large problem size.
# The command has been fixed to remove incorrect 'spack' calls and reduce the
# problem size to a small, testable scale as requested.
# The manifest adheres strictly to the MiniCluster specification, as required.
apiVersion: flux-framework.org/v1alpha2
kind: MiniCluster
metadata:
  name: amg2023-cpunode-test
  namespace: default
spec:
  # The MiniCluster will run on a single node.
  size: 1

  # The job will run with 4 MPI tasks.
  tasks: 4

  # Strict logging is enabled for detailed output.
  logging:
    strict: true

  # The pod will not be deleted after completion to allow for log inspection.
  cleanup: false

  # Defines the application container to be run by Flux.
  containers:
    - image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/fractale-agent-experiments:amg2023
      # FIX: The command is corrected to run AMG with problem type 2.
      # The problem size is reduced to a small value (-n 4 4 4) to prevent OOM errors.
      # The processor grid (-P 2 2 1) is set to match the 4 tasks for this small test run.
      # 'spack' and 'mpirun' are not used, as Flux handles the MPI environment.
      command: amg -problem 2 -n 4 4 4 -P 2 2 1

      # This is not a launcher-based job. This setting MUST be false.
      launcher: false

# This corrected manifest addresses the previous failure. The primary issue was
# a typo in the apiVersion ('valpha2' instead of 'v1alpha2').
# This version also resets the job to a small-scale test run as requested,
# reducing the problem size and task count to establish a working baseline.
# Debugging fields like backoffLimit and restartPolicy from the previous
# attempt are retained as they aid in analyzing failures.
apiVersion: flux-framework.org/v1alpha2
kind: MiniCluster
metadata:
  name: amg2006-cpunode-test
  namespace: default
spec:
  # The MiniCluster will run on a single node.
  size: 1
  # The number of tasks is reset to 4 for this baseline test run.
  tasks: 4

  # Pod-specific configurations for debugging.
  pod:
    # Do not restart the pod on failure, so logs from the single run can be examined.
    restartPolicy: Never

  # Limit job retries to aid in debugging specific failures.
  backoffLimit: 1

  # The pod and its resources will not be deleted after the job completes.
  cleanup: false

  # Strict logging is enabled for detailed error reporting.
  logging:
    strict: true

  containers:
    - image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/fractale-agent-experiments:amg2023
      # FIX: The command is corrected to run a small problem size (-n 4 4 4)
      # as required for the test, preventing potential OOM errors from large sizes.
      # The processor grid (-P 2 2 1) is set to match the 4 tasks.
      command: amg -problem 2 -n 4 4 4 -P 2 2 1
      # This is not a launcher-based job. This setting MUST be false.
      launcher: false

import math
from typing import Dict, Any, Literal
import json

def evaluate_amg_run(
    # Problem size
    problem_size: Any,
    total_ranks: int,
    nodes_used: int,
    # Hardware constraints
    cores_per_node: int,
    memory_gb_per_node: int,
    threading_hint: int,
    current_fom: float,
    threshold: float = 0.90,
    ideal_fom_per_core: float = 4.5e8,
    efficiency_sweet_spot: float = 1.0e6,
    dofs_per_gb: float = 1.2e7,
    memory_safety_factor: float = 0.95
) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    """
    Args:
        problem_size (tuple): The 3D problem grid dimensions (e.g., Px, Py, Pz).
        total_ranks (int): The total number of MPI tasks used for the run.
        nodes_used (int): The number of compute nodes used for the run.
        cores_per_node (int): The number of physical CPU cores on a single compute node.
        memory_gb_per_node (int): The total system RAM in Gigabytes on a single compute node.
        threading_hint (int): Specifies the SMT/Hyper-Threading level to assume (e.g., 1 for no SMT, 2 for SMT).
        current_fom (float): The measured Figure of Merit (FOM) from the completed run.
        threshold (float): The performance goal, as a fraction of the theoretical maximum FOM (default 0.90).
        ideal_fom_per_core (float): A tuning constant for the max FOM of a single core (default 4.5e8).
        efficiency_sweet_spot (float): A tuning constant modeling communication overhead (default 1.0e6).
        dofs_per_gb (float): A tuning constant for the memory model (DOFs per GB of RAM, default 1.2e7).
        memory_safety_factor (float): A safety margin for memory usage (default 0.95).

    Returns:
        (dict): A dictionary containing 'decision', 'reason', 'strategy_hint', and 'metrics'.
    """   
    total_dofs = problem_size[0] * problem_size[1] * problem_size[2]
    if total_ranks == 0:
        return {"decision": "RETRY", "reason": "The number of tasks cannot be zero. Suggest using at least one task."}

    # --- 2. Calculate Theoretical Performance and Ratios ---
    dofs_per_rank = total_dofs / total_ranks
    max_cores_on_node = cores_per_node * threading_hint
    cpu_per_rank = max_cores_on_node // total_ranks if nodes_used == 1 else cores_per_node

    scaling_efficiency = math.tanh(dofs_per_rank / efficiency_sweet_spot)
    effective_fom_per_core = ideal_fom_per_core * scaling_efficiency
    theoretical_max_fom = effective_fom_per_core * total_ranks * cpu_per_rank

    performance_ratio = 0.0
    if theoretical_max_fom > 1e-9:
        performance_ratio = current_fom / theoretical_max_fom

    estimated_memory_gb = total_dofs / dofs_per_gb
    memory_utilization = estimated_memory_gb / (memory_gb_per_node * nodes_used)

    metrics = {
        "performance_ratio": round(performance_ratio, 3),
        "scaling_efficiency": round(scaling_efficiency, 3),
        "memory_utilization": round(memory_utilization, 3),
        "dofs_per_rank": int(dofs_per_rank),
        "theoretical_max_fom": f"{theoretical_max_fom:.2e}"
    }
    # --- 3. Decision Logic based on prioritized bottlenecks ---        
    # Primary STOP condition: Performance is good enough.
    if performance_ratio >= threshold:
        return {
            "decision": "STOP",
            "reason": f"Optimization goal reached. Current performance is at {performance_ratio:.1%} of the theoretical maximum, meeting the {threshold:.1%} threshold.",
            "metrics": metrics
        }

    # Primary RETRY condition: Memory is the bottleneck.
    if memory_utilization >= memory_safety_factor:
        return {
            "decision": "RETRY",
            "reason": f"Memory utilization is critically high at {memory_utilization:.1%}. The problem size is too large for the allocated memory. Suggest significantly reducing the problem size.",
            "metrics": metrics
        }

    # Secondary RETRY condition: Scaling is the bottleneck.
    if scaling_efficiency < 0.5: # Heuristic for "low" efficiency
         return {
            "decision": "RETRY",
            "reason": f"Scaling efficiency is low ({scaling_efficiency:.1%}), indicating the problem size per rank is too small. Suggest significantly increasing the problem size to provide more work per rank.",
            "metrics": metrics
        }

    # Tertiary RETRY condition: Cores are underutilized on a single node.
    if nodes_used == 1 and total_ranks < max_cores_on_node:
        return {
            "decision": "RETRY",
            "reason": f"The node is under-subscribed ({total_ranks}/{max_cores_on_node} tasks used). Suggest increasing the number of tasks to better utilize the hardware.",
            "metrics": metrics
        }

    # Default RETRY condition: Performance is simply not good enough yet.
    return {
        "decision": "RETRY",
        "reason": f"Performance is at {performance_ratio:.1%} of theoretical max, which is below the {threshold:.1%} threshold. Suggest moderately increasing the problem size to improve the work-per-rank and move closer to the optimal FOM.",
        "metrics": metrics
    }
